what: The constructor discovers customer visited facts and all location facts from semantic fact names, identifies the depot as the location without a visited predicate, and maps depot/customers to compact node indices. It parses grounded `visit` and `return-to-depot` operator names once and obtains their directed metric costs with `metric_operator_cost_from_initial_values`, producing a task-specific directed routing matrix. At evaluation, it reads the propositional state, identifies the current location and unvisited customers, then computes a directed nearest-neighbour completion visiting every remaining customer and finally returning to the depot. Reusable propositional and node-marking buffers avoid repeated large allocations.
why: CVRP search choices are primarily routing choices, and the grounded operators expose the routing matrix reliably even when travel-cost fluents have been compiled into derived variables. A nearest-neighbour completion is inexpensive at O(n^2) per state, depends strongly on the current endpoint and remaining customer set, and provides a substantially more informative estimate than customer counts or accumulated cost. It also preserves directed costs and includes the mandatory final depot return. Capacity-driven depot transitions are not explicitly predicted because capacity and demand constants are not reliably named after numeric compilation; actual via-depot costs still enter the search path cost g(s), while this heuristic supplies a robust routing completion estimate without unsafe assumptions.
